criteria.name: Q1 Quality attributes
criteria.reasoning: Performance and availability are well justified from the lunch-peak scenario. The performance scenario has all six parts and a measurable measure. The availability scenario has all parts, but its response measure is vague and not measurable.

evidence.quote: Response measure: the system should stay up most of the time.

criteria.name: Q2 Architectural style
criteria.reasoning: Clear modular-monolith recommendation. Trade-offs are specific to team size and known problems, and the downside is acknowledged.

evidence.quote: With five developers, running eight or ten services would mean more time spent on infrastructure than on features.
The trade-off I accept is that modules cannot be scaled independently

criteria.name: Q3 Availability calculation
criteria.reasoning: Parts (a) and (b) are correct with working. Part (c) is wrong: it uses payment-provider availability as overall availability and ignores the other three components. Correct overall availability is 99.80%, downtime 1.5 h/month.

evidence.quote: So the new availability of placing an order is 99.9975%, which reduces the downtime to 0.000025 × 720 = 0.018 hours

criteria.name: Q4 Resilience pattern
criteria.reasoning: Circuit Breaker is named, correctly explained, applied to the slow-provider outage, and includes tuning via failure threshold and wait period.

evidence.quote: When failures exceed a threshold (for example 50% of calls in 10 seconds) the breaker moves to Open

criteria.name: Q5 Consistency and availability
criteria.reasoning: Both choices are reasonable and concrete techniques are named. However, CAP is misapplied: partition tolerance is not optional, and favouring consistency during a partition sacrifices availability, not partition tolerance.

evidence.quote: so for payments we choose consistency and availability and give up partition tolerance.

criteria.name: Q6 Architecture decision record
criteria.reasoning: Context, Decision and Consequences are present and specific. Consequences are one-sided: only positive outcomes are listed, with no negative consequence.

evidence.quote: Consequences: Placing an order no longer waits for the outlet, so the response time improves.

criteria.name: Communication and format
criteria.reasoning: Headings and IEEE-style references are present. However, Question 2 is about 181 words, exceeding the 150-word limit.

evidence.quote: The trade-off I accept is that modules cannot be scaled independently, and a bug in one module can still crash the whole process.

technical_issues.issue: Uses payment-provider availability 99.9975% as overall order-placement availability; ignores the other three components. Correct end-to-end availability is 99.80% and downtime is 1.5 h/month.
Does not show the full end-to-end calculation for part (c), only the payment-provider calculation.

CAP theorem is misapplied: partition tolerance is not optional; during a partition one chooses consistency or availability. For payments, favouring consistency sacrifices availability, not partition tolerance.
Availability scenario response measure 'stay up most of the time' is not measurable.
Consequences list only positive outcomes; no negative consequence is given.
Answer is about 181 words, exceeding the 150-word limit.

overall: Strong Q2 and Q4, with correct Q3(a)(b). Q3(c) and CAP misuse are significant. Q1 availability measure, Q6 negative consequence, and Q2 word limit need fixing. Overall solid but not fully compliant.

feedback.summary: You have strong Q2 and Q4, with correct Q3(a)(b). The main gaps are Q3(c) end-to-end availability, CAP misuse in Q5, a non-measurable availability response measure in Q1, one-sided consequences in Q6, and Q2 over the word limit. Fix these specific issues to move from Proficient to Excellent in those criteria.
next_steps: Re-work Q3(c): compute end-to-end availability from all four components (not just the payment provider), show the full calculation, and report overall availability and downtime to the requested precision.

Revise Q5: state that partition tolerance is not optional; explain that during a partition you choose consistency or availability, and for payments consistency sacrifices availability—not partition tolerance.
Tighten Q1, Q6 and Q2: make the availability response measure measurable, add at least one negative consequence to Q6, and cut Q2 to 150 words or fewer while keeping the scenario-specific trade-offs.

criteria.C1: You justified performance and availability well from the lunch-peak scenario. Your performance scenario has all six parts and a measurable response measure. Your availability scenario has all parts, but “stay up most of the time” is not measurable. To reach Excellent, make both response measures measurable—for example, a specific uptime percentage or maximum downtime.
criteria.C2: Excellent: your modular-monolith recommendation is clear, and your trade-offs are specific to the five-developer team and known problems, with the downside acknowledged. To stay at Excellent, keep trade-offs scenario-specific and continue acknowledging the downside. (Watch the separate 150-word limit for Q2.)
criteria.C3: You got Q3(a) and (b) correct with working shown. In Q3(c) you used the payment-provider availability as the overall order-placement availability and ignored the other three components; the correct end-to-end availability is 99.80% with 1.5 h/month downtime. To reach Excellent, show the full end-to-end calculation for (c) combining all four components.
criteria.C4: Excellent: you named Circuit Breaker, explained its mechanism correctly, applied it to the slow-provider outage, and included tuning via failure threshold and wait period. To stay at Excellent, keep the mechanism, outage application, and at least one tuning or drawback consideration explicit.
criteria.C5: Your choices are reasonable and you named concrete techniques. However, CAP is misapplied: partition tolerance is not optional; during a partition you choose consistency or availability. For payments, favouring consistency sacrifices availability, not partition tolerance. To reach Excellent, correct the CAP explanation and tie each choice to the C-versus-A trade-off during a partition.
criteria.C6: Context, Decision and Consequences are present and specific to the scenario. The consequences are one-sided: you list only positive outcomes. To reach Excellent, add at least one negative consequence (for example, a cost, risk, or trade-off) while keeping the positive consequence.
criteria.C7: Headings and IEEE-style references are present. Question 2 is about 181 words, exceeding the 150-word limit. To reach Excellent, keep every answer within 150 words and maintain precise terminology and citations.
